per_question.question: What medical loss ratio (MLR) must Medicaid managed care organizations meet under federal law, and how does NC implement this requirement?
per_question.agent_answer:
Under federal law, Medicaid managed care plans do **not automatically have a universal mandatory minimum MLR**. What federal law requires is that states make each MCO, PIHP, and PAHP **calculate and report** an MLR. If a state **chooses** to impose a minimum MLR in its contracts, that minimum must be **at least 85%**. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.8](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

## Federal rule

### 1) Reporting/calculation duty
States must ensure through their contracts that each Medicaid managed care organization calculates and reports an MLR in accordance with the federal rule. That duty applies regardless of whether the state has imposed a minimum threshold. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.8(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

### 2) Minimum-threshold duty is conditional
A minimum MLR is required **only if the state elects to mandate one**. In that event, the minimum must be **equal to or greater than 85%**. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.8(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

### 3) State oversight and remittances
If a state imposes a minimum MLR, it must annually submit to CMS a summary of each plan’s MLR reporting, including the numerator, denominator, MLR achieved, member months, and any remittances owed. If the state requires remittances for failure to meet the state’s minimum MLR, the state must reimburse CMS for the federal share and report its methodology. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.74(a)-(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

## How North Carolina implements it

North Carolina’s implementation evidence here is the CHIP managed care state plan amendment text, which states that North Carolina assures its rates are designed to reasonably achieve a medical loss ratio, and that if an MCO, PIHP, or PAHP owes a remittance for not meeting the minimum MLR required by the state, North Carolina will reimburse CMS for the federal share and submit the required separate report describing the state/federal share methodology. [SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care, § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/22-0013-proposed-amendment-chip-managed-care/download?attachment)

## Bottom line

- **Federal law:** plans must **calculate and report** MLR; a **minimum MLR of at least 85%** applies only if the state elects to require one. [42 CFR Part 438, § 438.8](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)
- **North Carolina:** the retrieved NC implementation text shows the state has adopted the federal remittance/reporting framework and assures rates are designed to reasonably achieve an MLR. The excerpt I retrieved does **not clearly state the exact numeric minimum MLR in NC’s contract language**, only the consequences if a state-required minimum is not met. [SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care, § 3.3](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/22-0013-proposed-amendment-chip-managed-care/download?attachment)
